American MMA fans have improved over the last ten or twenty years. I'll give them that. At least they've learned how to cheer when a guy on the ground improves position.

But, the Japanese MMA fans have always been more educated on the sport. Their whole attitude when it comes to the sport is just so spot on yet at times the exact opposite of how American fans feel. For example, in Japan a submission is the ultimate win. Because you make your opponent lose in the most humiliating way. You didn't just clock them and knock them out. Anyone can get hit hard enough to go to sleep. Especially if they're caught on the button. But, when you submit you're completely conscious and aware of the action. You submit to their will. You admit defeat with your own hand. It's so much more shameful.

Americans only want to see KO's. They're completely unimpressed when Ronda goes out there and arm bars ten chicks effortlessly. Some people act like it's not even really fighting. It's hilarious how they have a complete lack of respect for the entire grappling game.

Another thing is the fan's reactions. In Japan silence = bad / noise = good. If it's a bad fight you can hear a pen drop in the arena. When is the last time you ever heard an American audience be perfectly silent during a fight? Can you imagine how big of a mind fuck that must be to the fighters? Thousands of people just sitting there staring at you making absolutely no sound at all. It would make you feel really awkward. It would motivate the shit out of you to create some action. I think this is a far more logical approach.

Also, Japanese fans aren't obsessed with Win/Loss records. The ONLY thing that matters to them is if you fought like a man. That's it! Nothing else matters. Did you fight? Did you try to win? Did you keep fighting even when things weren't looking good? Did you act like a bitch? Did you pussy out? Did you let him snap your arm or did you tap? Did you let the choke knock you out or did you look for an easy out? The only thing that matters is you gave it your all and you fought like a man. If you go out there and lose ten fights in a row. So long as you were never a pussy. They'll cheer for you just as loud during that tenth fight as they did your second. Because you were a man. That's a true MMA fan right there. It's why I love fighters like Matt Brown. Does he win every fight? No. Does fight like a true warrior and like a real man? Yes. Does ever give up, ever? No. That's why I love him and will always cheer for him no matter what.

I just wanted to vent a little. I was watching some PRIDE FC DVD's and it still amazes me how the Japanese fans are so educated on the sport and have so much respect for the fighters. It's like night and day when compared to the guys you see at Hooters in TapOut shirts.
The difference between Japanese MMA fans and American MMA fans.

I've only ever watched an MMA fight with groups of friends, most of whom were either in my Jiu-Jitsu club or had some other connection to grappling. Certainly more educated than the average viewer, and of course we had a bias towards grappling/submissions. We still enjoyed watching the rest of the fight, but we definitely got loudest during the groundwork.

I've never had the misfortune to watch a fight at hooters, and from the sound of it I'm pretty fortunate.

The worst is the way the American fans chant, "USA! USA!" I shit you not. I've once heard a crowd do that when BOTH fighters were from America. I also heard them do it once when NEITHER fighter was American.

After going to Hooters twice we started going to a Casino. Much better and I don't gamble so I get to spend all my money on beer.

I love going to see fights live. I'm going to see Cormier vs Gustafsson in Houston and I'm super psyched. I don't mind the crowds, it reminds me of watching fights in the school yard. I love KOs. Honestly, how can you not like a KO? It is literally separating a person from their senses and their will. There's absolutely no question who won a fight when someone gets KO'd.

Don't get me wrong, I applaud a good submission, but I'd be lying if I said I'd rather see a submission win than a KO. I get the technical aspect of the fights and I do enjoy it. But nothing gets you pumping at a visceral, primal level like watching a man beat another man senseless in hand to hand combat. It's fucking exciting and I don't apologize for enjoying it.

It really depends what events and environments you watch attend in America. I went to Bellator 106 (Alvarez vs. Chandler 2) and it was a great atmosphere. Most of it made up of old school fans who originally bought tickets for Tito/Rampage before it was cancelled, and lots of people who were there for the local fights on the undercard. I also went to Bellator 85 and the crowd was great as it was full of people supporting local fighters. Those two events had the best fans out of any event (regional or major like UFC) and it's because of those factors (long term fandom, people who train supporting their teammates) that made them standout as great.

With the way the sport has grown, I'm expecting that more major markets will end up having fans becoming more educated as time goes on and there will be a ripple effect. The American crowds will never be like Japanese crowds, but I see them becoming a little more respectful than they were 10 years ago.
